title: Assay Timing Control
purpose: Verified ACR behaviour, reviewed by Product, as input for writing a same-as-ACR specification.

requirements.text: For each time-dependent stage of the test flow, the software shall implement a defined start event, minimum duration, permitted completion window and expiry behaviour. These values shall be fixed in the application and shall not be configurable at run time.
requirements.document_note: Values TBD, to be established by the timing-flex study. Confirmed at review that the study completes before milestone 3 and is not needed for milestones 1 and 2, so the milestone-1 build enforces these windows against provisional values

requirements.text: The software shall record and persistently retain the start time of each time-dependent stage.

Following application backgrounding, screen locking, or any other temporary interruption, the software shall calculate elapsed time from the retained start time and shall not restart the applicable timer.
The software shall derive elapsed time from a time source that is not affected by user modification of the device clock or time zone.
requirements.document_note: Future development, formerly BL-24. Until implemented, the timing windows in section 12 can be defeated by changing the device clock, since elapsed time is derived from a source the user can alter. RA 4.18 relies on the timers being enforceable.

requirements.text: The software shall measure the time elapsed from the user's confirmation of sample collection to the connection of the Sample Pod to the Mixing Cartridge. If the elapsed time exceeds the defined limit, the software shall prevent the user from proceeding and display an explanatory error message.
requirements.document_note: Limit TBD, fixed not configurable; currently specified as 30 minutes. Timed silently in the background: no countdown is shown, so that the user is not hurried

requirements.text: The software shall present the coloured release button instruction only after both the required Incubation Well residence time has elapsed and the preceding user instructions have been completed.
If the coloured release button step is not completed within the permitted timing window, the software shall invalidate the test and prevent continuation.

The software shall prevent progression past any time-dependent stage before the applicable minimum time has elapsed, including preventing the Test Board from being scanned before the required colour-evolution period has elapsed. This shall not apply where the application is in demonstration mode, which produces no result for a patient.
The software shall permit the Test Board to be scanned only within the validated scanning-time window, and shall invalidate the test if that window has expired.
The software shall display, for each active time-dependent stage, the time remaining until the next action is permitted and the time remaining before the permitted window expires.
The software shall issue a local device notification when a timed window is about to expire, and shall do so only where the application is in the background at that time.
requirements.document_note: Local notification, not a backend push; see FR-COM-009

requirements.text: The software shall generate local device notifications without dependence on backend connectivity, for the purposes defined in FR-TIM-014.
requirements.document_note: Backend push notifications are future development as FR-COM-013

requirements.text: The software shall request the permission required to present device notifications, shall precede the platform permission prompt with an explanation of why notifications are wanted, and shall not prevent a test from being started, completed or reported if permission is refused.
requirements.document_note: Added at review. FR-TIM-014 and FR-COM-009 cannot function without this permission and nothing previously required it to be asked for. Milestone follows those two requirements

requirements.text: When a test is invalidated on timing grounds, the software shall inform the user of the reason and instruct the user to repeat the test with a new kit.

Where a timed waiting period is long enough, the software shall present within the instructional flow a card that displays the time remaining and whose content changes as the period elapses. The thresholds determining whether the card is presented shall be fixed in the application. Its content shall be optional, in that not reading it can affect neither the conduct nor the validity of the test, and the card shall yield whenever the flow requires the user to act.
requirements.document_note: The mechanism is what is required: a modal within the chat, opened by the flow rather than by the user, whose content is a function of elapsed time in the current stage. The content itself, currently tips presented in sequence, is part of the approved content set under FR-TXT-004 and can change without changing this requirement

scenarios.title: The stick clock from DIPPED IT to SCAN

lines.behaviour: Every timed stage uses values fixed in the app build; nothing about the timings is downloaded or changed at runtime.
lines.ios: Total stick time (180 s), countdown (70 s) and the sample window (900 s) are compile-time constants for the Minuteful Kidney US target.
lines.android: The same values are build flags for the US flavour (180 s, 75 - 5 s); the sample window is a hard-coded constant.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-001's second sentence — timing values fixed in the application, not configurable at run time — is exactly ACR's arrangement: every duration in the timed flow is settled when the build is made, and no server value or runtime setting can reach any of them.

lines.behaviour: The stick clock starts the moment the user taps DIPPED IT, not when the stick touches urine.
lines.ios: The dip confirmation tap starts a 180-second clock held in memory.
lines.android: The dip confirmation tap stores the dip time on disk and arms a 180-second expiry.
lines.relation_note: The stage has the defined start event FR-TIM-001 requires — the user's confirmation tap, not the physical dip — and FR-TIM-002's recording happens at that instant on both platforms. Whether the record then persists differs by platform and is judged at the interruption lines.

lines.behaviour: After dipping, a button counts down '75 SECONDS TO GO' and turns into SCAN when it reaches zero.
lines.ios: The button shows the remaining count and becomes tappable only when the displayed count reaches zero.
lines.android: The button shows the remaining count and becomes clickable only when the count reaches zero.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-001 asks only that a minimum duration exist; ACR goes further and shows it as a live countdown, which is the first half of FR-TIM-005 — the time remaining until the next action is permitted — delivered prominently. The second half of FR-TIM-005, time remaining before the window expires, appears nowhere.

lines.behaviour: The countdown shows 75 seconds but runs for 70 real seconds, so SCAN appears about five seconds before 75 have passed.
lines.ios: Each displayed second lasts about 0.93 real seconds: 70 real seconds are stretched over 75 displayed ones.
lines.android: Identical arithmetic: 70 real seconds counted down from 75, one tick every 933 milliseconds.
lines.relation_note: The displayed minimum and the enforced minimum deliberately differ: 75 counted units elapse in 70 real seconds so the user reaches the camera as the stick becomes scannable. FR-TIM-001's minimum is enforced downstream at the true value, but the display FR-TIM-005 would rely on does not measure real seconds.

lines.behaviour: Photos taken before 75 seconds since dipping are not used; the camera keeps looking until the stick is ready.
lines.ios: Frames arriving before 75 seconds are discarded silently and another frame is requested; no message is shown.
lines.android: Frames arriving before 75 seconds are handed to the compiled analysis engine flagged as not-yet; what the engine does with them is not readable.
lines.relation_note: The minimum duration is genuinely enforced where it matters: no image captured before the minimum is ever used, which is FR-TIM-008's prevention of early progression applied to FR-TIM-001's minimum. On one platform the final say lives inside a compiled component, but the observed rule holds on both.
lines.pm_comment: No dipping in QACR. will be relevant for the detection timer

lines.behaviour: Once SCAN appears the user has until 180 seconds after dipping to finish scanning; no on-screen clock shows the time left.
lines.ios: After the countdown ends the button simply reads SCAN; the remaining window is not displayed anywhere.
lines.android: After the countdown ends the button simply reads SCAN; the remaining window is not displayed anywhere.
lines.relation_note: The permitted completion window FR-TIM-001 requires exists — from the minimum to 180 seconds after the start event — but once the countdown ends nothing shows how much of it remains, so FR-TIM-005's display of time before expiry is absent exactly where it would matter.
lines.pm_comment: No dipping in QACR. scan time window still TBD

lines.behaviour: About 90 seconds after dipping a chat bubble says 'Click Scan now. The stick will expire in 90 seconds.'
lines.ios: The scanning-stage bubbles are paced by fixed delays that sum to roughly 89 seconds before this bubble.
lines.android: Different per-bubble delays, but they also sum to roughly 89 seconds before this bubble.
lines.relation_note: The only statement of remaining time the user ever gets is a scripted sentence timed to be true when it appears; FR-TIM-005 asks for a display of the time remaining before the window expires, and a fixed phrase that would silently become false if the window or pacing changed is at best a stand-in for one.
lines.pm_comment: No dipping in QACR, will be elaborated on the bubbles structure doc

lines.behaviour: When results are produced successfully the stick clock is cleared; the next test starts a fresh clock.
lines.ios: The clock is stopped when the on-device analysis succeeds.
lines.android: The dip time is cleared when the analysis succeeds, and again whenever the home screen appears.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-002 says the start time shall be recorded and persistently retained but not when the record may end; ACR's answer — discard at success, fresh clock for the next test — is a reasonable reading the requirement never states.

lines.behaviour: The screen stays awake for the whole test, so the countdown is never hidden by the lock screen.
lines.ios: The idle timer is disabled for the entire app session.
lines.android: Every test screen keeps the display on while it is in front.
lines.relation_note: Keeping the screen awake for the whole test is what makes the countdown and the timed messages actually visible, and no requirement in the corpus mentions the display's sleep behaviour at all; without it the timed flow would spend most of its life behind the lock screen.

scenarios.title: The three minutes run out

lines.behaviour: If 180 seconds pass before a successful scan, an alert says 'Time Is Up — You can no longer use the stick for this test.'
lines.ios: A blocking alert with a single button.
lines.android: A non-dismissible alert with a single button.
lines.relation_note: The stage's defined expiry behaviour — FR-TIM-001's fourth element — is a blocking alert that names the consequence, the beginning of FR-TIM-012's obligation to tell the user why the test ended; it fires identically whether the deadline passes in the chat or during capture.

lines.behaviour: The alert's only button reads 'Continue' on iOS and 'CONTINUE' on Android.
lines.ios: Button label: Continue.
lines.android: Button label: CONTINUE.
lines.relation_note: The expiry behaviour is the same in substance on both platforms, but the one word every timed-out user reads is cased differently on each; trivial, yet it is a visible seam in what FR-TIM-001 treats as one defined behaviour.
lines.pm_comment: Should have a method to standardize text style and capital letters

lines.behaviour: Tapping the button opens a troubleshooting chat headed STICK NO LONGER VALID explaining that more than 3 minutes have passed since dipping.
lines.ios: The timeout troubleshooting script opens with that section and bubble.
lines.android: The same troubleshooting script and strings open.
lines.relation_note: Expiry opens a guided recovery that states the reason — more than three minutes since the dip — which is FR-TIM-012's informing done well; the conversation that follows goes beyond anything FR-TIM-001's 'expiry behaviour' or FR-TIM-012's instruction describes.

lines.behaviour: The troubleshooting chat asks whether the stick was removed from its wrapping and offers YES / NO answers.
lines.ios: Two buttons: YES, I EXTRACTED THE STICK / NO, I DID NOT EXTRACT IT, each leading to its own follow-up.
lines.android: Same two buttons and follow-ups.
lines.relation_note: Asking whether the stick ever left its wrapping, with two answers leading to different fates for the kit, is recovery logic no timing requirement contemplates; it exists because the deadline can expire before anything was physically spent, a case the corpus never addresses.

lines.behaviour: The expiry alert can interrupt the instructions chat and the camera; on Android it can also interrupt the analysis screen.
lines.ios: Once the scan is handed to analysis the alert is disarmed; an analysis that outlives the window continues.
lines.android: The analysis screen re-arms the same deadline and shows the timeout if it passes before results.
lines.relation_note: The platforms disagree about where the permitted completion window ends: one closes it when capture completes and lets a long analysis finish, the other keeps enforcing it into analysis and can fail a test whose images are already taken. FR-TIM-001's 'defined window' and FR-TIM-011's expiry thus have two ends, one per platform.

lines.behaviour: If the clock expires while the camera is open, scanning stops and the same Time Is Up alert appears.
lines.ios: Frame requests stop and the camera view enters an error state; the alert is presented by the flow.
lines.android: The preview is hidden and the alert is shown over the camera.
lines.relation_note: Expiry is enforced during capture, not merely before it: the camera stops and the same defined expiry behaviour appears mid-scan, so the window genuinely bounds the whole act of scanning as FR-TIM-011 requires.

lines.behaviour: After a failed scan the user rescans under the original clock; if it has already lapsed, Time Is Up appears at once.
lines.ios: On returning to the camera the remaining time is checked immediately.
lines.android: On the camera appearing, a passed deadline is processed immediately.
lines.relation_note: FR-IMG-015 permits re-scanning after a failed capture, and FR-TIM-003 forbids restarting the timer; ACR gives retries exactly that shape — every rescan runs under the original clock, and a rescan attempted after the window has lapsed meets the expiry immediately.

lines.behaviour: An expired attempt is recorded as timed out and, in this build, whatever was captured is still uploaded for review.
lines.ios: Timeout upload is set to always for Minuteful Kidney US.
lines.android: The upload-on-timeout flag is on for the ACR FDA product.
lines.relation_note: Marking the order timed out and still uploading whatever was captured is data handling the timing requirements never mention; the invalidated attempt has an afterlife — review, reporting, kit consequences — that no corpus requirement currently owns.

scenarios.title: Backgrounding, lock, calls and process death

lines.behaviour: Leaving the app during the countdown does not reset it; on return it shows the correct remaining time.
lines.ios: Remaining time is recomputed from the recorded start instant when the app returns.
lines.android: Remaining time is recomputed from the recorded start instant when the screen resumes.
lines.relation_note: This is FR-TIM-003 verbatim: leaving the app does not restart anything, and the countdown shown on return is recomputed from the retained start instant, so the elapsed time is derived, not resumed.

lines.behaviour: If the three minutes elapse while the app is away, Time Is Up appears immediately on return.
lines.ios: On return, a non-positive remaining time is reported as expiry at once.
lines.android: On resume, a passed deadline fires the expiry at once.
lines.relation_note: An expiry that fell due during the absence is honoured the moment the app returns — remaining time is derived from the retained start, found negative, and the expiry behaviour fires at once, with no credit given for time spent away.

lines.behaviour: Locking the screen or taking a call behaves like backgrounding: the visible countdown pauses, the underlying clock keeps running.
lines.ios: Going inactive pauses only the button's ticking; elapsed time is arithmetic on the start instant.
lines.android: Pausing the screen stops only the button's ticking; elapsed time is arithmetic on the start instant.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-003 names screen locking and other temporary interruptions alongside backgrounding, and ACR treats them identically: only the visible ticking pauses, while elapsed time remains arithmetic on the start instant, so a call or a locked screen costs the user nothing but the view.

lines.behaviour: If the system kills the app mid-wait, Android restores the countdown and deadline; iOS forgets the dip and restarts from the home screen.
lines.ios: The clock start is held only in memory; nothing about it is written to disk.
lines.android: The dip time is saved in encrypted storage and the countdown start is saved with the screen state.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-002's persistent retention exists on one platform only: one writes the start to durable storage and can restore the countdown and deadline after a system kill, the other holds it in memory and forgets the dip entirely — half the product meets the requirement and half does not.
lines.pm_comment: full kill of the app mid wait should reopen to the lobby with alert confirmation if the user used the kit or not (same as timeout troubleshooting)

lines.behaviour: If the user force-quits and relaunches mid-wait, both apps open at the home screen with no memory that a stick was dipped.
lines.ios: Nothing about the clock was persisted.
lines.android: The dip time survives on disk but the home screen clears it as it appears.
lines.relation_note: After a force-quit both platforms present a home screen with no memory of the dipped stick — one because nothing was persisted, the other because the persisted start is wiped as the home screen appears. FR-TIM-002's retention is thus defeated even where it exists, and FR-STA-007's identify-and-invalidate on reopening has nothing to work from on either platform.
lines.pm_comment: full kill of the app mid wait should reopen to the home screen with alert confirmation if the user used the kit or not (same as timeout troubleshooting)

lines.behaviour: Coming back after more than 15 minutes away normally restarts the app from the beginning, but not while a stick clock is running.
lines.ios: The restart is suppressed whenever the clock has a start time.
lines.android: The restart is suppressed while the timer is running or has already timed out.
lines.relation_note: Suppressing the idle restart while the clock runs is FR-STA-003's no-inactivity-timeout term honoured for this stage; partly, because the corpus makes a test active from the control that starts it, and the same protection is denied to the earlier stages of the same active test.

lines.behaviour: The scanning-stage bubbles keep pace with real time even if the user leaves the app, so 'expire in 90 seconds' stays roughly accurate.
lines.ios: Real-time bubbles keep being scheduled while the chat is suspended.
lines.android: On return, bubbles whose time has passed are inserted at once.
lines.relation_note: The scripted timing copy stays roughly truthful because pacing follows real time rather than time in the foreground, which is FR-TIM-003's derivation applied to content; but FR-STA-002 forbids delivering instructional content while backgrounded and asks for resumption from the point reached, and one platform keeps scheduling items while suspended, so the two platforms resume by different rules.

lines.behaviour: If the countdown's end has already passed when the chat is shown again, the button appears immediately as SCAN.
lines.ios: A recomputed display time of zero enables the button without ticking.
lines.android: A recomputed time-left of zero finishes the timer without ticking.
lines.relation_note: When the countdown's end passed during the absence, the control appears already unlocked — the derived elapsed time drives the button's state directly, with no replaying of the missed ticks, which is precisely the calculate-from-retained-start rule.

scenarios.title: Clock edges, defaults and clock changes

lines.behaviour: All stage clocks read the phone's clock; setting it forward expires the stick early and setting it back extends the window.
lines.ios: Every clock compares wall-clock instants; no monotonic time source is used.
lines.android: Same, through a thin time service that still returns wall-clock time.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-004 requires a time source the user cannot move; every stage clock in ACR reads the device's wall clock, so setting it forward expires the stick early and setting it back extends the window indefinitely. Nothing of the requirement's substance is delivered — its own notes record it as future development, and ACR is the state those notes describe.
lines.pm_comment: futue requirement (M5) to use a different clock

lines.behaviour: Changing only the time zone does not affect any clock; the app compares absolute instants, not local times.
lines.ios: Seconds since a fixed reference date are compared.
lines.android: Milliseconds since the epoch are compared.
lines.relation_note: The time-zone half of FR-TIM-004 is genuinely met: both platforms compare absolute instants, so changing the zone moves nothing. Only the clock half — the one with teeth — is unmet, which makes this the one corner of the requirement ACR already satisfies.

lines.behaviour: Expiry is noticed only when a screen checks; nothing fires while the app is closed — no alarm, no notification.
lines.ios: No local notification is scheduled for the end of the window.
lines.android: No alarm, scheduled work or foreground service exists in the app.
lines.relation_note: Deriving elapsed time on return satisfies FR-TIM-003's letter, and the requirement demands nothing proactive; but the consequence is that expiry is only ever noticed when a screen looks — no alarm or notification exists — so the user who stays away learns of the expiry only by coming back.

lines.behaviour: The 180-second and 75-second values exist only because this build overrides the product-wide defaults of 120 and 60 seconds.
lines.ios: Defaults are 120 and 55 (+5) seconds; Minuteful Kidney US sets 180 and 70 (+5).
lines.android: Defaults are 120 and 60; the flavour sets 180 and 75.
lines.relation_note: The values are fixed in the application as FR-TIM-001 requires, but 'the application' is one variant of a family: the same code carries different defaults that this product overrides, so the fixed values are per-variant facts a release engineer sets, not constants of the product's design.

lines.behaviour: On iOS, after an analysis fails for a non-quality reason, the next test that session may run without the Time Is Up cutoff.
lines.ios: Static reading: the clock is not cleared after firing unless explicitly stopped, and a new start then skips scheduling; unconfirmed at runtime.
lines.android: No equivalent: the deadline is re-derived from the stored dip time on every screen.
lines.relation_note: A static reading of one platform suggests the expiry mechanism may not be re-armed for the next test after certain failures, silently removing FR-TIM-001's defined expiry behaviour for that run; unconfirmed at runtime, but a defined behaviour that can lapse without trace is a defect in the very definition the requirement asks for.

not_knowable_from_code.what: What the Android analysis engine does with frames handed to it before 75 seconds have passed since dipping (flagged as read-only).
not_knowable_from_code.why: The flag is passed into a compiled native library; whether such frames are ignored, used for alignment only, or counted cannot be read from the app.

not_knowable_from_code.what: Whether the iOS stale-clock defect (boundary-5) actually suppresses the Time Is Up alert for a second test in the same session.
not_knowable_from_code.why: The reading is static: a fired one-shot timer is kept referenced, so a later start skips scheduling unless the app was backgrounded in between. Only a run through analysis-failure then a new test settles it.

not_knowable_from_code.what: Whether Android's restore of the countdown after a system-initiated process kill works end to end.
not_knowable_from_code.why: It depends on the saved screen state being handed back by the OS and the chat re-reading it; the dip time itself is on disk, but the countdown restore path is only exercised at runtime.

not_knowable_from_code.what: What the server does with an order marked client-timed-out and with the uploaded timed-out scan.
not_knowable_from_code.why: Both apps only send the status and the capture; the consequences (new kit, support ticket, reporting) live in the backend.

not_knowable_from_code.what: Whether an old iOS install can carry a persisted wait time that differs from the build value.
not_knowable_from_code.why: The minimum-wait setting is decoded from persisted settings with a legacy fallback; only inspecting a device upgraded from an older version shows whether a stale value survives.

not_knowable_from_code.what: Exact real-time drift of the paced scanning bubbles on a device.
not_knowable_from_code.why: Pacing is delays plus audio durations plus rendering; the 89-second sum is arithmetic on the script, not a measurement.

scenarios.title: From CUP IS FULL to DIPPED IT within 15 minutes

lines.behaviour: Tapping CUP IS FULL silently records the time; nothing on screen shows a clock or countdown for the sample.
lines.ios: The tap is time-stamped in memory; the chat continues to the stick section unchanged.
lines.android: The tap is time-stamped and saved to disk; the chat continues unchanged.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-006 measures elapsed time from the user's confirmation of sample collection, and its note asks for silent background timing so the user is not hurried; ACR stamps the confirmation tap and shows no clock or countdown, which is exactly that starting point handled exactly that way.

lines.behaviour: The sample must be dipped within 15 minutes of confirming the cup is full.
lines.ios: 900 seconds, a literal in the flow set-up.
lines.android: 15 minutes in milliseconds, a named constant.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-006 requires a defined limit and FR-TIM-001 requires such values to be fixed in the application; both platforms carry the same fixed figure. ACR's limit is 15 minutes where the corpus currently notes 30 — a value choice for the timing study, not a difference of shape.

lines.behaviour: The 15-minute check happens only when the user taps DIPPED IT; there is no warning as the limit approaches.
lines.ios: The comparison runs inside the dip-tap handling and nowhere else.
lines.android: The comparison runs inside the dip-tap handling and nowhere else.
lines.relation_note: The requirement asks that elapsed time be measured and the user prevented from proceeding only if the limit is exceeded, timed silently per its note; checking once, at the moment the user tries to proceed, with no approaching-limit warning, is a faithful reading of that.

lines.behaviour: Within the limit, tapping DIPPED IT starts the stick clock and the 75-second countdown as usual.
lines.ios: Valid sample → scanning section is triggered and the stick clock starts.
lines.android: Valid sample → dip time stored, expiry armed, scanning section triggered.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-006 defines only the failure side — prevent and explain when the limit is exceeded; the within-limit case, where the confirmation passes straight through into the next timed stage, is the requirement's unstated complement rather than anything it asks for.

lines.behaviour: The sample check exists only in the US build; other builds of the same product skip it entirely.
lines.ios: Enabled by a per-target flag that is off by default and on for Minuteful Kidney US.
lines.android: Enabled by a build flag that is off by default and on for the the US flavour flavour.
lines.relation_note: The requirement is unconditional: the software shall measure and enforce the sample age limit. In ACR the entire check exists only in the US build of the product and other variants skip it, so the requirement describes one build's behaviour, not the software's.

scenarios.title: The sample is older than 15 minutes

lines.behaviour: After more than 15 minutes, tapping DIPPED IT shows 'Urine sample expired' and explains the sample should be tested within 15 minutes.
lines.ios: A blocking alert with that title and body.
lines.android: A non-dismissible alert with the same title and body.
lines.relation_note: This is the requirement's failure branch operating as written: the elapsed time exceeded the limit, the user is prevented from proceeding by a blocking alert, and the message explains the condition — the sample should have been tested within the limit.

lines.behaviour: The alert also says this kit can no longer be used and offers to send a new one.
lines.ios: Body: "…This kit can no longer be used, we will be happy to send you a new one."
lines.android: Same body.
lines.relation_note: The explanation goes beyond FR-TIM-006's error message into FR-TIM-012's ground: the user is told the reason and that this kit is finished, and a new kit is promised. FR-TIM-012 asks for an instruction to repeat the test with a new kit; ACR instead offers to send one, which commits the backend to a remedy the requirement never mentions.

lines.behaviour: The alert's only button opens Support; it reads 'Support' on iOS and 'SUPPORT' on Android.
lines.ios: Button: Support → support screen.
lines.android: Button: SUPPORT → support screen.
lines.relation_note: FR-SUP-003 requires support contact to be presented where the software blocks the user and the condition is not theirs to resolve; an expired sample is exactly such a block, and the alert's only action opens support. The button's casing differs between platforms, a copy divergence only.

lines.behaviour: The stick clock never starts and the countdown never appears; the test cannot continue with this kit.
lines.ios: In the expired branch the dip tap neither starts the clock nor advances the chat to the scanning section.
lines.android: In the expired branch no dip time is stored and the scanning section is not triggered.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-006's 'prevent the user from proceeding' is realised structurally: the next timed stage is simply never entered — no clock starts, no countdown appears — so there is nothing to bypass and no path onward with this kit.

lines.behaviour: The attempt is recorded as 'sample expired', and afterwards the app treats this kit as used up.
lines.ios: The order is marked sample-expired locally before the alert.
lines.android: The order is marked sample-expired locally and counted as a failed test.
lines.relation_note: Recording the attempt as an expired sample and treating the kit as spent goes beyond FR-TIM-006's wording, which stops at preventing and explaining; but that durable record is the material FR-KIT-007 depends on when the next test attempt must be met with a message matched to the previous test's outcome.

lines.behaviour: After Support, the user lands back on the home screen rather than in the test.
lines.ios: The flow is dismissed with a support request; finishing support ends the flow.
lines.android: Support is opened with return-to-home on finish.
lines.relation_note: That the user lands at the home screen with no path back into the test makes FR-TIM-006's prevention permanent, but the requirement says nothing about where the user goes after the error, so the routing is ACR's own resolution of a question the corpus leaves open.

scenarios.title: Leaving, locking or losing the app before dipping

lines.behaviour: Leaving the app between CUP IS FULL and DIPPED IT does not pause the 15 minutes; the original tap time is used.
lines.ios: The stored tap instant is compared with the dip instant; backgrounding changes nothing.
lines.android: The stored tap instant is compared with the dip instant; backgrounding changes nothing.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-003 requires elapsed time to be calculated from the retained start after any temporary interruption, never restarted; ACR compares the original confirmation instant with the completion instant regardless of backgrounding, which is that rule applied to FR-TIM-006's measurement.

lines.behaviour: If the app is killed after CUP IS FULL, iOS forgets the tap and the check is skipped; Android keeps the time on disk.
lines.ios: The tap time lives only in memory; with it gone, the dip tap proceeds as if the sample were fresh.
lines.android: The tap time is persisted; a system restore of the screen keeps the check intact.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-002 requires the start time of each time-dependent stage to be persistently retained. Android retains this one on disk; iOS holds it only in memory, so if the process dies before the completion tap the freshness check silently disappears and an old sample passes — the safeguard FR-TIM-006 asks for stops existing exactly when it is hardest to notice.

lines.behaviour: Being away for more than 15 minutes before dipping restarts the app from the home screen, so the expiry alert is rarely reached that way.
lines.ios: The idle restart applies because no stick clock is running yet.
lines.android: Same rule; and the home screen then clears the recorded tap time.
lines.relation_note: FR-STA-003 forbids any inactivity timeout while a test is active, and a test is active from the control that starts it; ACR still applies its idle restart at this stage because no stick clock runs yet. The restart shares the 15-minute threshold, so most users who exceed the sample limit while away meet the home screen instead of FR-TIM-006's explanatory error.

scenarios.title: Edges of the 15-minute window

lines.behaviour: At exactly 15 minutes iOS still allows dipping; Android already treats the sample as expired.
lines.ios: Expired only when elapsed is strictly greater than 900 seconds.
lines.android: Valid only while elapsed is strictly less than 15 minutes.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-006 speaks of one defined limit, but at exactly the limit the platforms disagree — one still accepts the sample, the other already rejects it. Practically invisible, yet it means the limit's own definition differs between the two implementations of the same rule.

lines.behaviour: Setting the phone's clock back extends the 15 minutes; setting it forward shortens them.
lines.ios: Both instants come from the wall clock.
lines.android: Both instants come from the wall clock via a thin time service.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-004 requires elapsed time to come from a source the user cannot move; both platforms measure this window on the device's wall clock, so setting the clock back extends the limit and setting it forward shortens it. Nothing of the requirement is delivered — its own notes record it as future development, and ACR is the state those notes describe.

lines.behaviour: Before the alert, no chat bubble or screen mentions the 15-minute rule; the alert is the first the user hears of it.
lines.ios: The only occurrence of '15 minutes' in this target's copy is the alert body.
lines.android: The only occurrence of '15 minutes' in this flavour's copy is the alert body.
lines.relation_note: Silence while timing is what FR-TIM-006's note asks for, but ACR extends it further than the note requires: the limit is never mentioned anywhere until it is broken, so the first the user hears of the rule is the alert that ends their kit — a product choice the requirement neither asks for nor forbids.

lines.behaviour: The 15-minute value is fixed in the app and cannot be changed without a new release.
lines.ios: A literal in code.
lines.android: A constant in code.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-001 requires timing values to be fixed in the application and not configurable at run time, and FR-TIM-006's note says the limit is fixed, not configurable; the value is baked into each build and can change only with a release, on both platforms.

not_knowable_from_code.what: What the server does with an order marked 'client expired urine sample' (new kit shipment, support ticket, reporting).
not_knowable_from_code.why: Both apps only record the status and route the user to Support; the promise 'we will be happy to send you a new one' is fulfilled, if at all, outside the apps.

not_knowable_from_code.what: Whether Android's persisted tap time actually survives a system-initiated process kill through to the dip tap.
not_knowable_from_code.why: The tap time is on disk, but whether the user is returned to the same chat position (so that a dip tap can happen) depends on the saved screen state being restored by the OS; only a run settles it.

not_knowable_from_code.what: Whether the expired-sample alert is ever shown to real users in practice.
not_knowable_from_code.why: The idle restart uses the same 15-minute threshold, so the reachable cases are narrow (stayed in the app, or short absences adding up); frequency is an analytics question, not a code question.

scenarios.title: Dip confirmed, wait, SCAN unlocks

lines.behaviour: Tapping DIPPED IT starts one three-minute test clock; the SCAN control appears at once below the chat, locked, showing a countdown.
lines.ios: The dip confirmation starts the single shared test clock for 180 seconds and fires the event that admits the countdown control into the chat.
lines.android: The dip confirmation stamps the dip time (a 180-second window is derived from it) and fires the same event that admits the countdown control.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-007 asks that the release instruction be presented only after the residence time has elapsed; ACR presents the control immediately but locked, counting down, so the instruction is withheld in effect though visible from the first second. The countdown itself is the display FR-TIM-005 requires of the time remaining until the next action is permitted.

lines.behaviour: The locked SCAN control cannot appear before the dip is confirmed; each earlier step needs its own confirmation first.
lines.ios: The scanning section of the script is admitted only by the dip-confirmation event; the preceding kit, cup, urine, stick and dip steps each end in a button.
lines.android: Same script, same gating event, same per-step buttons.
lines.relation_note: The other half of FR-TIM-007 — that the preceding user instructions be completed first — is delivered structurally: the section holding the release control is admitted only by the dip confirmation, and every earlier step ends in a confirmation of its own, so the control cannot exist before the procedure has actually been walked.

lines.behaviour: The countdown starts at "75 SECONDS TO GO" and reaches zero after about 70 real seconds.
lines.ios: The control is told to run for 70 seconds while displaying 75 units, so each displayed second lasts about 0.93 real seconds.
lines.android: The control is told to run for 75 minus a 5-second offset (70 seconds) while counting from 75; tick interval is 933 ms.
lines.relation_note: The stated residence time is 75 seconds but the control unlocks after 70, the displayed count running about seven percent fast to hide the difference; FR-TIM-007's 'only after the residence time has elapsed' is met five seconds short, deliberately, as a head start for opening the camera, and FR-TIM-005's displayed remaining time is not measured in real seconds.

lines.behaviour: A coloured fill sweeps across the control as it counts; at zero the label becomes SCAN and the control becomes tappable.
lines.ios: A progress view widens linearly over the remaining run time; touch is enabled only once no display time remains.
lines.android: A revealing layout animates its clip to full width over the remaining run time; the button becomes clickable when the tick count reaches zero.
lines.relation_note: The unlock — the fill completing, the label changing, the control becoming tappable — is ACR's presentation of the release instruction, so FR-TIM-007's gated moment exists and is unmistakable; but it arrives at the shortened seventy seconds rather than after the stated residence time, so the letter of 'only after' is not quite kept.

lines.behaviour: During the wait nine timed messages arrive: why the wait is needed, a scanning demo video, distance advice, then "We're ready. Let's scan."
lines.ios: Nine real-time script items with fixed pauses, one of them a replayable video, each with a voice clip.
lines.android: Same nine items and copy; pauses come from a resource table with two values differing by about a second from iOS.
lines.relation_note: What fills the wait is scripted narration with a demonstration video — content FR-TIM-007 never mentions. The corpus instead fills a timed wait with FR-IMG-022's practice scan, an interactive rehearsal of the scanning interaction; ACR's watch-only video is the ancestor of that idea, not its equal, so the waiting period's content is a departure the mapping should not blur.

lines.behaviour: "We're ready. Let's scan." appears roughly 70 seconds after the dip, about when the control unlocks.
lines.ios: Summed pauses put the message at about 69.4 seconds plus a second or two of untimed items.
lines.android: Summed pauses put the message at about 69.6 seconds plus the untimed first echo, roughly 71–72 seconds.
lines.relation_note: The 'ready' instruction lands at roughly the moment the control unlocks, which reads as FR-TIM-007 satisfied; but the message follows its own scripted pauses and nothing links it to the gate, so the instruction is presented near the elapsed time rather than because of it.

lines.behaviour: Roughly 90 seconds after the dip a reminder appears: "Click Scan now. The stick will expire in 90 seconds."
lines.ios: The last real-time item, 20 seconds after the ready message (about 89–91 s after dip); it also reports an analytics event.
lines.android: Same item, same copy, about 91–92 seconds after dip.
lines.relation_note: A reminder half-way through the window goes beyond FR-TIM-009, which names only the invalidation; and as the sole statement of remaining time it is a fixed sentence that happens to be true at the moment it appears, not the live display of time before expiry that FR-TIM-005 requires.

lines.behaviour: Tapping SCAN records how long the user waited and opens the scanner; nothing else is checked at that moment.
lines.ios: The tap sends an analytics event with elapsed seconds and dismisses the chat successfully; the scanner is pushed.
lines.android: The tap sends two analytics events (click, elapsed seconds) and launches the scanner.
lines.relation_note: Tapping the unlocked control records how long the user waited and reports the step — a slice of FR-ANL-001's required analytics of progress through the flow. The timing requirements themselves are silent here, and deliberately so: no check runs at this tap, because expiry would already have fired if the window had closed.

scenarios.title: SCAN never tapped inside three minutes

lines.behaviour: If SCAN is not tapped within 180 seconds of the dip, a blocking alert appears: "Time Is Up", the stick is unusable.
lines.ios: The shared clock posts an end notification; the test flow shows the timeout alert with title, body and a single Continue button.
lines.android: A scheduled task fires at the remaining time; the chat screen shows a non-dismissible error alert with the same title, body and CONTINUE.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-009 requires the test to be invalidated when the release step is not completed within the window, and this is that moment: 180 seconds after the dip with the control untapped, a blocking alert announces the stick can no longer be used, on both platforms, however the app is currently occupied.

lines.behaviour: The test is marked timed out; Continue leaves the chat for a troubleshooting conversation headed STICK NO LONGER VALID.
lines.ios: Order status is set to client timeout before the alert; Continue stops the clock and replaces the chat with the timeout troubleshooting flow.
lines.android: Order status is set to client timeout; CONTINUE clears the timeout flag and opens the troubleshooting screen for a timeout.
lines.relation_note: Invalidation and prevention are both real: the order is marked timed out before the alert, and the only way forward replaces the test conversation with a recovery flow headed by the stick's invalidity — the user cannot continue, and FR-TIM-012's obligation to explain begins immediately.

lines.behaviour: Troubleshooting says more than 3 minutes passed since dipping and asks whether the stick was taken out of its wrapping.
lines.ios: Two bubbles then a two-option button; both scripted in the target's troubleshooting script.
lines.android: Identical script and copy.
lines.relation_note: Naming the cause — more than three minutes since the dip — is FR-TIM-012's informing done properly; the follow-up question about whether the stick ever left its wrapping goes beyond both requirements, existing because the deadline can pass before the stick was ever exposed, a case the corpus does not contemplate.

lines.behaviour: YES, I EXTRACTED THE STICK leads to ORDER NEW KIT: the kit is single-use and the only exit is TO CUSTOMER SUPPORT.
lines.ios: For this variant (not single-kit) the answer changes nothing further; the next group ends in a support button.
lines.android: Same script; whether the order is additionally marked a confirmed failure depends on a backend-supplied single-kit flag.
lines.relation_note: For a stick that was exposed, continuation is genuinely impossible — the kit is declared single-use and the only exit is customer support for a new one — which is FR-TIM-009's prevention carried to its end and FR-TIM-012's instruction that the test be repeated with a new kit.

lines.behaviour: NO, I DID NOT EXTRACT IT marks the attempt a dry run, says the kit is still valid, and offers BACK TO HOME VIEW.
lines.ios: Order status is set to dry run; the closing group tells the user to keep the stick wrapped and return later.
lines.android: Same status change and same closing group.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-009 says invalidate and prevent continuation; ACR lets the user reverse that verdict by answering that the stick never left its wrapping, whereupon the attempt becomes a dry run and the kit is declared valid, verified by nothing but the answer. A recovery the requirement does not contemplate, resting entirely on self-report.

lines.behaviour: After the 90-second reminder there is no further warning before the alert; the clock simply runs out.
lines.ios: The reminder is the final item of the scanning section of the script.
lines.android: Same: nothing follows the reminder in the script.
lines.relation_note: After the single mid-window reminder the clock simply runs out, and the first the user hears of the expiry is the alert itself; FR-TIM-009 asks for exactly that invalidation and nothing more, so the absence of escalation is the requirement operating as written rather than a gap in it.

scenarios.title: Dip confirmed too long after the sample

lines.behaviour: Confirming the dip more than 15 minutes after confirming the full cup shows "Urine sample expired" instead of starting the clock.
lines.ios: The urine-step confirmation is timestamped; at dip confirmation a 900-second comparison decides between starting the clock and the expiry alert. Enabled for this target only.
lines.android: Same 15-minute comparison from the cup timestamp; enabled by a build flag that is on for this flavour only.
lines.relation_note: This is FR-TIM-006's sample-age check seen from the dip side of the seam: the elapsed time from the sample-collection confirmation is measured at the dip confirmation, and past the limit the user is prevented from proceeding with an explanatory error instead of a started clock. Neither of this feature's own requirements mentions it, but the corpus covers it.

lines.behaviour: That alert offers only SUPPORT; the attempt is recorded as an expired sample and the user goes to customer support.
lines.ios: Order status is set to expired urine sample; the single button dismisses the chat with a support request.
lines.android: Same status; the single button opens the support screen and returns to the lobby afterwards.
lines.relation_note: The support-only exit is FR-SUP-003 working — the user cannot resolve an expired sample themselves, and support contact is the single action offered; recording the attempt as an expired sample goes beyond FR-TIM-006's wording, though it is what makes the failure durable rather than momentary.

scenarios.title: Backgrounding, quitting and relaunching during the wait

lines.behaviour: Leaving the app during the wait does not pause anything; on return the countdown shows the true remaining time.
lines.ios: The clock recomputes remaining time from its start timestamp on foreground; the countdown view re-derives its display from its own start date.
lines.android: The dip time is a wall-clock stamp; the countdown view recomputes progress from it each time the chat reappears.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-003's rule — derive elapsed time from the retained start, never restart — is exactly how both platforms handle leaving the app mid-wait: the countdown shown on return is computed from the original dip instant, and FR-TIM-009's window keeps running in real time throughout.

lines.behaviour: Messages that fell due while the app was in the background appear all at once on Android; iOS has no catch-up step.
lines.ios: The chat engine keeps scheduling real-time items one interval at a time even while suspended; there is no bulk insertion on resume, so overdue items arrive one by one.
lines.android: On reappearing, the engine walks the real-time items, inserting every item whose interval has already elapsed in one bulk update.
lines.relation_note: FR-STA-002 requires that instructional content not be delivered while the application is in the background and that delivery resume from the point reached; one platform resumes with a bulk catch-up of everything overdue, while the other keeps scheduling items even while suspended and its on-screen behaviour after a long absence is unconfirmed, so the two resume differently and only one clearly matches the requirement.

lines.behaviour: If the three minutes run out while the app is in the background, Time Is Up appears immediately on return.
lines.ios: On foreground the clock reports expiry at once when remaining time is negative.
lines.android: On reappearing, a non-positive remaining time triggers the expiry handler immediately.
lines.relation_note: An expiry that fell due while the app was away is honoured the moment the user returns: remaining time is recomputed from the retained start, found negative, and the invalidation fires at once — FR-TIM-003's derivation feeding FR-TIM-009's consequence with no grace granted for the absence.

lines.behaviour: Closing the chat during the wait asks "You already dipped the stick" — quitting will require a new kit — with Quit and Stay.
lines.ios: The dismiss control raises the critical cancel alert once the dip has been confirmed.
lines.android: The back gesture raises the after-dipping cancel alert once the dip time is set.
lines.relation_note: FR-STA-008 requires that a cancellation requested after the sample is committed be met with a warning that the test cannot be resumed and a new kit will be needed, plus explicit confirmation; the quit-after-dip alert says precisely that and offers exactly the stay-or-quit choice the requirement describes.

lines.behaviour: Choosing Quit ends the test and returns home; nothing is recorded about the dipped stick, and no failure is logged.
lines.ios: The clock is stopped and the flow ends; the order status is left untouched.
lines.android: The lobby is re-opened; on appearing it clears the dip time; the order status is left untouched.
lines.relation_note: Of FR-STA-010's three obligations on a confirmed cancellation, two are met — the test cannot be resumed and the user returns to the start — but the third, invalidating the active test, never happens: the order's status is left untouched and no record exists that a dipped stick was abandoned, so the kit's fate is unwritten anywhere but analytics.

lines.behaviour: While the clock is running, returning from the background never resets the app to its start screen, as it otherwise can.
lines.ios: The foreground reset check is told the user is in a critical path whenever the clock has a start time.
lines.android: The idle-reset rule is skipped while the dip clock runs or a timeout is pending.
lines.relation_note: FR-STA-003 forbids any inactivity timeout while a test is active, and while the stick clock runs ACR honours that: the idle restart is suppressed on both platforms. Partly, because a test is active from the control that starts it, and this protection begins only at the dip — the earlier stages of the same active test still lose to the idle reset.

lines.behaviour: After the app is killed and relaunched, the dipped stick is forgotten: no deadline is enforced and a new test can start.
lines.ios: The clock lives only in memory; nothing persists its start time.
lines.android: The dip time is persisted, but the home screen clears it as soon as it appears.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-002 requires the stage start to be retained persistently and FR-STA-007 requires a reopened app to identify and invalidate the incomplete test; one platform never persists the start, the other persists it and then wipes it at the home screen, and neither looks for the incomplete test at all — so a killed app forgets the dipped stick and a fresh test can begin as though nothing happened.

scenarios.title: Edges of the window

lines.behaviour: The chat says "wait 75 seconds", the countdown starts at 75, yet SCAN unlocks after 70; displayed seconds run about 7% fast.
lines.ios: Display units are scaled: 75 units over 70 seconds.
lines.android: Tick interval is 933 ms so 75 ticks complete in 70 seconds.
lines.relation_note: The chat promises a 75-second wait, the counter starts at 75, and the gate opens after 70 real seconds because each displayed second lasts about 0.93; FR-TIM-005's displayed remaining time is therefore systematically wrong by design, and FR-TIM-007's residence time is shortened by the same five seconds the scanner later withholds from capture.

lines.behaviour: The 180-second deadline counts from tapping DIPPED IT, not from the countdown reaching zero or from tapping SCAN.
lines.ios: The clock is started in the dip-confirmation handler.
lines.android: The dip timestamp is written in the dip-confirmation handler and every window is derived from it.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-001 requires each timed stage to have a defined start event, and FR-TIM-009's window has one: the dip confirmation, from which the whole 180 seconds is measured on both platforms — not the countdown's end, not the tap on the unlocked control — so every later moment has a single unambiguous origin.

lines.behaviour: All three durations — 70-second countdown, 75-second minimum, 180-second deadline — are fixed in the build; the server cannot change them.
lines.ios: Per-target build variables give 70 and 180; the 5-second camera allowance is a code constant; a legacy stored copy exists but is not fed by the server.
lines.android: Flavour build fields give 180 and 75 with a default 5-second offset.
lines.relation_note: All three durations that govern this stage are fixed in the build and cannot be changed at run time, which is FR-TIM-001's second sentence exactly; no server value, remote configuration or user setting reaches any of them on either platform.

lines.behaviour: In demo mode there is no countdown: every step is inserted at once and a plain SCAN button is offered immediately.
lines.ios: A demo-skip branch of the script adds all groups at once, scrolls to a plain button and never starts the clock.
lines.android: Same script branch; the timer control receives no data in demo mode.
lines.relation_note: In demonstration mode the wait disappears: every step is inserted at once and a plain, immediately tappable control replaces the countdown. FR-TIM-008 exempts demonstration mode from minimum-time gating, so presenting FR-TIM-007's release instruction without its residence time is the exemption working as granted.

lines.behaviour: The "We're ready" message and the SCAN unlock are timed separately; neither triggers the other.
lines.ios: The message follows scripted pauses; the control follows its own run time; nothing links them.
lines.android: Same: scripted pauses versus the control's own tick schedule.
lines.relation_note: The 'ready' instruction and the unlock are two independent timelines tuned to coincide — scripted pauses on one side, the control's own schedule on the other, with nothing connecting them; FR-TIM-007's 'only after' is thus achieved by arithmetic that happens to agree today, and either side can drift without the other noticing.

not_knowable_from_code.what: What the backend does with the client timeout, expired-sample and dry-run order statuses (for example whether the kit's code is blocked from reuse after a timeout, or freed after a dry run).
not_knowable_from_code.why: Both apps only record the status locally and send it with later requests; the consequences are decided server-side.

not_knowable_from_code.what: Exact on-screen pacing of wait messages on iOS after a long background: whether overdue messages appear at once or one by one with their normal delays.
not_knowable_from_code.why: The engine keeps scheduling real-time items while suspended using run-loop timers; how those timers fire on resume is runtime behaviour.

not_knowable_from_code.what: Whether demo mode (long-press on start) is switched on for real Minuteful Kidney US users.
not_knowable_from_code.why: It is gated by a server-supplied flag delivered at sign-in; the apps default it to off outside debug builds.

not_knowable_from_code.what: Whether, on Android, answering YES I EXTRACTED THE STICK additionally marks the order a confirmed failure.
not_knowable_from_code.why: That branch depends on a single-kit flag that the backend can override at initialisation; iOS reads a fixed false for this target.

not_knowable_from_code.what: Whether the iOS Time Is Up alert can be dismissed by any means other than Continue.
not_knowable_from_code.why: The alert component's dismissal behaviour was not read; Android's alert is explicitly non-dismissible.

not_knowable_from_code.what: The exact real-time position of each wait message after the dip.
not_knowable_from_code.why: Only the scripted pauses are data; the untimed items in between depend on voice-clip durations resolved at runtime.

scenarios.title: Scanning inside the window

lines.behaviour: SCAN opens the scanner about 70 seconds after the dip; the scanner starts searching for the Color-Board immediately.
lines.ios: The chat dismisses successfully and the scanner is pushed; on appearance the camera starts and a new exam is begun with no time check.
lines.android: The scanner screen is launched; on creation, because the dip clock is running, the scan session and preview start at once.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-008 prevents progression past the stage before the minimum has elapsed; ACR lets the user into the scanner five seconds early and starts searching at once, so the stage is enterable before the minimum even though capture — the act the requirement protects — is still withheld.

lines.behaviour: Until 75 seconds have passed since the dip, no image is captured even with the Color-Board framed; the user sees no message.
lines.ios: Each processed frame is discarded until elapsed time since the dip reaches 75 seconds; the scanner simply requests the next frame.
lines.android: Each frame is handed to the image-processing engine in read-only mode until 75 seconds have elapsed since the dip.
lines.relation_note: The requirement forbids the board being scanned before the colour-evolution period has elapsed, and this is that prohibition in force: until the minimum is reached every frame is discarded or processed read-only, so no image can be captured however well the board is framed. The requirement names the outcome, not the mechanism, and the outcome holds on both platforms.

lines.behaviour: From 75 seconds on, images are captured normally; results only ever come from images taken after the minimum time.
lines.ios: Once elapsed time reaches the threshold, up to three frames with different torch settings are added to the exam.
lines.android: Once the minimum has passed, frames are processed for real and collected until the engine reports collection complete.
lines.relation_note: From the minimum onward capture proceeds normally and results only ever come from images taken after it — the lower bound of FR-TIM-011's validated window and the end of FR-TIM-008's prevention, meeting exactly where the requirements say they should.

lines.behaviour: Each captured image is stamped with how many seconds had passed since the dip.
lines.ios: Per-frame metadata carries elapsed seconds derived from the shared clock.
lines.android: The exam frame record carries elapsed seconds derived from the dip timestamp.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-011 asks that scanning be permitted only within the window; stamping every captured image with the seconds elapsed since the dip goes further, making compliance evidenced per image rather than merely enforced. No corpus requirement asks for that timing record, though downstream review of window compliance would rest on it.

lines.behaviour: Once the images are captured and analysis begins, the three-minute deadline no longer interrupts the user.
lines.ios: The scanner signals it is about to finish, which disables the timeout alert; the scanner also stops listening to the clock.
lines.android: The analysis screen has no timeout alert at all; see the boundary scenario for what it does record.
lines.relation_note: The requirement says the board may be scanned only within the window and the test invalidated when it expires; ACR reads 'scanned' as 'captured', so once the images exist the deadline stops interrupting the user even though the clock is still running. Where the window ends is thus ACR's interpretation, not the requirement's words.

scenarios.title: Deadline passes while scanning

lines.behaviour: If 180 seconds pass while the scanner is open, scanning stops and "Time Is Up — you can no longer use the stick" appears.
lines.ios: The clock's end notification makes the scanner save a timed-out attempt, stop the camera and show an error overlay; the test flow shows the alert.
lines.android: The next processed frame sees no time left: preview stops, a timed-out attempt is recorded and the scanner shows the same alert.
lines.relation_note: This is the upper bound of FR-TIM-011 enforced inside the scanner itself: when the window expires mid-scan, capture stops, the attempt is recorded as timed out, and a blocking alert tells the user the stick can no longer be used.

lines.behaviour: The timed-out attempt, with whatever images exist, is still uploaded for quality review; the user is not told.
lines.ios: This target always uploads a timeout exam, including a processing trace.
lines.android: This product flavour has timeout upload enabled: the engine dumps its pipeline and the attempt is queued.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-011 says invalidate; ACR additionally keeps whatever images exist and uploads the timed-out attempt for quality review without telling the user. No requirement covers retaining or transmitting the data of a failed attempt, so behaviour with real privacy and expectation consequences currently has no home in the corpus.

lines.behaviour: Continue leads to the same STICK NO LONGER VALID troubleshooting as timing out in the chat.
lines.ios: The same coordinator-level alert and troubleshooting route as F05.3.
lines.android: The scanner's alert routes to the troubleshooting screen for a timeout.
lines.relation_note: The invalidation FR-TIM-011 requires flows into the recovery FR-TIM-012 describes: the user is told the stick is no longer valid because too long has passed, and the conversation ends in new-kit guidance — the same route whether the deadline passed in the chat or in the scanner.

lines.behaviour: Returning to the scanner after a framing warning once the deadline has passed shows Time Is Up instead of the camera.
lines.ios: Re-entry after a boundary result checks remaining time on appearance and shows the timeout alert if negative.
lines.android: On creation with the timeout flag set, the preview is hidden behind an overlay and the timeout handling runs.
lines.relation_note: FR-IMG-015 permits re-scanning after an invalid image only while the window lasts, and FR-TIM-011 forbids scanning beyond it; re-checking the window on every scanner entry delivers both — a user returning from a framing warning inside the window may try again, and one returning after the deadline meets the timeout instead of the camera.

lines.behaviour: Android notices the deadline only when an image result returns; iOS reacts the instant the clock ends.
lines.ios: A one-shot clock notification is observed by the scanner.
lines.android: The check runs after each processed frame; there is no scheduled trigger inside the scanner.
lines.relation_note: Both platforms enforce the deadline, but one is told the instant the clock ends while the other only notices when the next processed frame returns; ordinarily a one-frame delay, but if frames stop arriving the expiry is never noticed inside the scanner on that platform, so the requirement's guarantee rests on the camera staying healthy.

scenarios.title: Scanning before the minimum

lines.behaviour: The scanner cannot be opened early from the chat: the SCAN control stays locked until its countdown ends.
lines.ios: Touch on the control is disabled while display time remains.
lines.android: The button is not clickable until the tick count reaches zero.
lines.relation_note: The control that opens the scanner cannot be used while its countdown runs, which is FR-TIM-008's prevention made visible: the user is physically unable to begin the scan for the first seventy seconds, and the remaining five are covered by the capture gate inside the scanner.

lines.behaviour: No too-early check exists at scanner entry; the 5-second gap is covered by withholding capture, not by a message.
lines.ios: Neither the flow that pushes the scanner nor the scanner's appearance handler compares elapsed time against the minimum.
lines.android: The chat launches the scanner unconditionally; the scanner checks only whether the clock is running or expired.
lines.relation_note: The requirement's prevention holds, but nothing at scanner entry checks the minimum — the gap is closed silently in the capture path alone, with no message. The user is blocked without ever being told a block exists, and the enforcement lives in one place rather than at the doorway the user actually walks through.

scenarios.title: Demonstration mode

lines.behaviour: Demo mode is entered by long-pressing the start button on the home screen, when the backend allows it or in debug builds.
lines.ios: A long press on the lobby start button is accepted when the build is debug or a server-supplied flag is on.
lines.android: A long press on the start-another-test control is accepted when the server flag (defaulting to the debug setting) is on.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-008 presumes a demonstration mode exists — it exempts one — but says nothing about how it is reached; ACR's answer is a hidden long press on the home screen, allowed in debug builds or when the backend permits it, which is behaviour the corpus neither requires nor constrains.

lines.behaviour: In demo mode capture starts immediately on both platforms; only Android still enforces a deadline, 105 seconds after opening the scanner.
lines.ios: The clock is never started, so no minimum and no deadline apply.
lines.android: Opening the scanner back-dates the dip by 75 seconds: the minimum is already met and 105 seconds of the 180 remain.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-008 lifts the minimum in demonstration mode and is silent about the completion window, as is FR-TIM-011; ACR's platforms resolved that silence differently — one applies no deadline at all in demo, the other still ends the demo scan after a shortened window — so the same words currently describe two behaviours.

lines.behaviour: Demo mode bypasses the 75-second minimum on both platforms: iOS by never starting the clock, Android by back-dating the dip.
lines.ios: With no clock start, the frame gate treats elapsed time as unknown and allows capture.
lines.android: The back-dated dip makes elapsed time read 75 seconds at once.
lines.relation_note: The requirement says the minimum shall not apply in demonstration mode, and on both platforms it does not: capture is available the moment the demo scanner opens, each platform arranging that by its own means. The exemption the requirement grants is delivered.

scenarios.title: Leaving and re-entering the scanner

lines.behaviour: Backgrounding while scanning keeps the deadline running; returning after it has passed shows Time Is Up.
lines.ios: On foreground the clock reports expiry immediately and the scanner handles it.
lines.android: The next processed frame, or re-creation of the scanner, finds no time left.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-003 requires elapsed time to be derived from the retained start across interruptions, and FR-TIM-011 requires the window to hold; backgrounding mid-scan changes nothing, and a user returning after the deadline meets the timeout at once rather than a revived camera.

lines.behaviour: Closing the scanner with its X returns to the chat; the clock keeps running and SCAN can be tapped again.
lines.ios: Cancel pops back to the chat, whose unlocked control is still displayed; the clock is untouched.
lines.android: Back closes the scanner; the chat reschedules its own timeout for the remainder and restores the finished control as clickable.
lines.relation_note: FR-TIM-011 says only when scanning is permitted, so ACR's answer — leave and re-enter the scanner as often as you like while the window lasts, with the clock untouched — is a consequence the requirement implies but never states: the window belongs to the stick, not to the attempt.

scenarios.title: Edges of the scanning window

lines.behaviour: The scanning window is 75 to 180 seconds after the dip on both platforms; both ends are fixed in the build.
lines.ios: 70-second target value plus a 5-second code constant; 180-second target value.
lines.android: 75-second and 180-second flavour build fields.
lines.relation_note: The validated window FR-TIM-011 names is 75 to 180 seconds after the dip on both platforms, and per FR-TIM-001 both ends are fixed in the build and untouchable at run time; the two platforms assemble the same numbers by different means, but the numbers are the same.

lines.behaviour: If analysis is still running when the deadline passes, Android records the test as timed out with no message; iOS records nothing.
lines.ios: After the scanner hands off, the timeout alert is disabled and the scanner stops listening; the clock's end has no further effect.
lines.android: The analysis screen schedules the remaining time and, if it fires before the algorithm succeeds, marks the order timed out and sets the timeout flag silently.
lines.relation_note: The platforms disagree about what the window's expiry means once capture has succeeded but analysis is still running: one records the test as timed out silently, the other records nothing and lets the analysis finish. A slow but successful scan is a completed test on one platform and a logged failure on the other, so FR-TIM-011's 'invalidate' has two meanings at this edge.

lines.android: Same numbers; frames are processed read-only meanwhile.
lines.relation_note: For up to five seconds the scanner is open, apparently working, and silently capturing nothing; FR-TIM-008's prevention holds, but FR-TIM-005 — which requires the time remaining until the next action is permitted to be displayed — would have this residue of the wait shown, and the scanner shows nothing but its normal framing guidance.
